Progress in anticancer chemical constituents and pharmacological research of Carpesium cernuum L. (Review).

This review compiles the anticancer chemical constituents of the medicinal plant Carpesium cernuum L., cataloging its bioactive compounds and their pharmacological effects and molecular targets. It integrates literature and experimental data to map the molecular network underlying the plant's anticancer mechanisms, while noting current research limitations. The work aims to provide a reference for developing novel anticancer drugs from this plant source.

Plant biotechnology journal 2026-12-01 Medium

Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.

This paper describes how the CABBI center used a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn framework to engineer C4 grasses (such as sorghum, sugarcane, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol (oil) in vegetative tissues rather than just seeds. By coordinating molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program, the authors show how such cross-disciplinary integration can accelerate progress toward renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals. The work offers lessons on organizing large-scale bioenergy engineering efforts around iterative DBTL cycles.

Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.

This study examines how the specificity of EEG-related Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms affects phenotype-driven gene scoring and variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. The authors investigate whether using more or less specific EEG terms changes the ranking of candidate genes, providing guidance for deep phenotyping in clinical genomics.

Nucleic acids research 2026-11-20 High

LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.

LACA is a new database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets from 134 species with information on their maximum lifespans, covering over 148 million cells and 190 annotated cell types. It enables researchers to compare cellular and molecular programs across species to uncover mechanisms underlying longevity and aging. The resource addresses the lack of systematic connections between single-cell gene expression and species lifespan.

PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.

PRGdb 5.0 is a major update to the Plant Resistance Genes database, expanding it to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins across 279 plant proteomes, including 288,315 newly predicted resistance-associated proteins. The curated reference set of experimentally supported resistance proteins grew from 199 to 462, and the platform adds AI-assisted prioritization to complement domain-based classification. This provides plant biologists with a unified resource for discovering and exploring disease resistance genes.

The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.

The mOTUs database has been updated to version 2027, expanding genome coverage for understudied environments and adding functional annotations to its 3.9 million genomes. It now includes a hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates for samples, enabling customizable grouping and linking of taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography. This resource helps researchers connect microbial community composition to functional potential even when cultured representatives are lacking.

A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation.

The authors present a graph-based computational framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA–mRNA interactions, orthology relationships, and functional annotations across multiple bacterial species to enable comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation. This approach addresses the difficulty of resolving sRNA evolutionary dynamics when sequence conservation is limited, allowing detection of functional conservation even among unrelated sRNAs that regulate similar processes.

CellStressDB: an AI-powered database of cellular responses to physical stressors.

CellStressDB is a new AI-powered database that compiles transcriptomic data on how cells respond to physical stressors, covering 131 studies with over 2.3 million single-cell and 1,205 bulk observations from human and mouse across nine stress classes and 21 tissue categories. It organizes these data into 2,848 indexed analysis entries, providing a centralized resource for exploring stress-response programs in signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate.

A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.

This paper presents a cell-type-resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation screen to identify gene regulatory effects underlying systemic lupus erythematosus and related immune phenotypes. The authors emphasise rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and multiple-testing correction before biological interpretation, addressing the limitations of whole-blood eQTL analyses that average regulatory effects across leukocytes.

PDBe in 2027: integrating literature annotations, molecular dynamics data, and AI-ready access.

PDBe has expanded its structural database by integrating residue-level annotations mined from more open-access literature, adding cross-links to molecular dynamics simulation data, and introducing AI-ready access methods. These updates make experimentally determined biomacromolecular structures more richly contextualized and easier for both researchers and computational tools to use.

ONITH: An ontology-based non-clinical integration and term harmonization pipeline for data reuse in 3R.

ONITH is a pipeline that integrates non-clinical animal study data and harmonizes terminology using ontologies, aiming to make existing animal data more reusable in line with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace). By standardizing terms across heterogeneous sources, it supports data-driven drug development while reducing the need for new animal experiments.

Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.

The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells, enabling uncertainty-quantified simulation of metabolic perturbations. Metabolic control analysis revealed 28 enzyme-level vulnerabilities, 24 of which map to existing or approved drugs, and independent DepMap data supported the predictions. The work shows that multi-omics-constrained kinetic modeling can quantify pathway rewiring and prioritize metabolic drug targets in a genotype-specific manner.

PANTHER: the protein tree and function resource in 2027.

PANTHER is a database of phylogenetic trees for protein-coding gene families, with branches manually annotated with Gene Ontology terms that model how protein functions evolved over time. These evolutionary models are used to propagate GO annotations to genes and to classify orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs. This paper reports updates to the resource since its 2022 publication, including expanded database content.

PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.

PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.

ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that integrates disease module identification and drug repurposing prediction by coordinating specialized AI agents over heterogeneous biomedical data and networks. It aims to lower the barrier to in silico repurposing by letting users interact in natural language while agents handle data integration and analysis. InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.

InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign sequences to families and predict domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, giving extensive coverage of UniProtKB and linking to resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central reference for protein function annotation across the life sciences.

Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.

The paper introduces bionSBM, a graph-based topic modelling method for integrating single-cell multi-omic data (transcriptome, epigenome, surface proteins). It combines community-detection on multipartite graphs with topic modelling to cluster and interpret high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data. The approach aims to provide a more comprehensive view of cellular properties by jointly analyzing multiple molecular layers.

Functional Analysis of GarCIPK8 from Gossypium aridum Conferring Salt Stress Tolerance in Gossypium hirsutum.

The authors transferred GarCIPK8, a salt-responsive kinase gene from a wild diploid cotton species, into cultivated upland cotton and found that overexpressing lines grew markedly better under high-salinity (300 mM NaCl) conditions. This suggests that the CBL-CIPK signaling pathway can be harnessed through transgenic approaches to improve salt tolerance in an important crop.

Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.

This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps induced by the two strains showed distinct proteomic programs, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in skin immunity.

Reactive astrocyte subpopulations with high Gfap and C4b expression in different Alzheimer's disease mouse models: Single-cell nuclear transcriptome analysis.

This study used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to profile hippocampal tissue from multiple Alzheimer's disease mouse models at early disease stages, focusing on reactive astrocyte heterogeneity. The authors identified distinct reactive astrocyte subpopulations characterized by high expression of Gfap and C4b, revealing cell-type-specific transcriptional changes that bulk transcriptomics had obscured. The findings highlight conserved and model-specific astrocyte states that may contribute to early AD pathogenesis.

Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.

This perspective argues that AI-driven multi-modal data analysis should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements. Under this view, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology while AI supplies the quantitative inputs, potentially reshaping how mechanistic drug-development models are built and parameterized.

PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.

PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps UniProt protein sequences to PDB structures at residue-level resolution. It improves on the original SIFTS pipeline by using MMseqs2 for fast sequence search, a better scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and refinement based on backbone connectivity. This makes high-quality structure-function mapping accessible to any lab without relying on internal PDBe infrastructure.

Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.

This study combined cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) with two ensemble machine learning methods, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Machine, to identify informative SNP markers associated with body weight in broiler chickens at hatch and 3 weeks of age. The approach demonstrates that GBS plus ML can serve as a cheaper alternative to high-density SNP arrays for genome-wide association studies in poultry breeding. The work highlights candidate markers that could inform selection programs for growth traits.

Dingent: A Configurable Agent Framework for Biological Database Retrieval and Integration.

Dingent is an open-source framework that lets developers wrap biological database functions as tools and compose them into explicit, configurable multi-step retrieval workflows, with administrators configuring assistants and users querying in natural language. It provides data-access plugins, directed workflows, and web interfaces, and was benchmarked against a single-assistant tool-calling baseline. The work targets the practical engineering problem of coordinating resource-specific tools and instructions across heterogeneous biological databases.
